hypotheses.statement: Current ClayCode G9 semantics can realize bounded host-resource lifetime safety through typed FFI/runtime lowering using existing CapabilityToken/ResourceRef/effect boundaries; no DB-specific core primitive is required for this slice.
evidence: WebAssembly Component Model opaque own/borrow resource handles
hypotheses.falsifier: A real ClayCode application or FRANK component requiring resource lifetime behavior that cannot be represented through existing typed ResourceRef/capability/effect semantics plus runtime ABI/FFI.

hypotheses.statement: Host-resource validity must include freshness/capability epoch or equivalent generational identity; opaque handle identity alone is insufficient against stale reuse.
evidence: epoch-check ablation accepted stale handle when the check was removed
parallel ABA worker tests slot-reuse identity as a complementary failure mode
hypotheses.falsifier: A target backend whose generative handle semantics provably prevent all stale reuse without an explicit or implicit freshness/generation mechanism.

hypotheses.statement: Borrow/ownership lifetime must be enforced either statically, dynamically, or both; allowing owner close while a borrow remains live creates an executable safety counterexample.
evidence: borrow-close ablation changed rejection into acceptance
Component Model dynamically tracks borrows/lends and enforces drop conditions
hypotheses.falsifier: A backend/translation proof showing equivalent lifetime safety without borrow tracking because stronger ownership constraints make the state unreachable.

hypotheses.statement: Resource type identity must survive lowering; an untyped opaque integer/handle is insufficient because cross-resource misuse becomes executable when the type check is removed.
evidence: type-check ablation accepted db handle as file handle
Component Model resource types are generative and classify handle kinds
hypotheses.falsifier: A lowering that erases resource type identity yet proves cross-kind substitution impossible by a stronger independently verified mechanism.

counterhypotheses.statement: The final backend already supplies all lifetime/freshness/type guarantees, so ClayCode/runtime metadata would be redundant and should not duplicate them.
A static affine type checker can make runtime borrow/freshness checks unnecessary for all trusted lowering paths.
Capability epoch belongs only to effect authorization, not resource identity; tying them could spuriously invalidate long-lived resources.

decision: Do not change ClayCode syntax/core semantics from this run. Specify/test a backend-neutral ResourceHandle lowering contract in CC-WP-07 and require target-specific translation validation.
